summary: Round 3 review of all 15 units. Both round-2 fixes hold: the nonlinear-sources worked example and q003 now state a high-strength alloy (yield above 800 MPa) assumed linear elastic, and the root stresses of 240 MPa and 222 MPa recompute correctly; q003 key 12.346 percent is right. The fe-modal rule of thumb (about 10 to 20 linear elements per wavelength, 5 to 10 per half wavelength) is now consistent, and my own eigenvalue computation for the consistent-mass fixed-fixed bar (closed-form dispersion relation) gives 10.27, 2.59, 1.65, 0.64, 0.41 and 0.10 percent at 2, 4, 5, 8, 10 and 20 elements per half wavelength, matching the fix agent and supporting the lesson's 1.7 and 0.4 percent and the factor-of-four claim. The two-element statement (errors about 2.5 and 22 percent) corresponds to the fixed-free bar with LUMPED mass (-2.55 and -21.58 percent); the consistent-mass fixed-free bar gives +2.59 and +19.46 percent. The lesson states this correctly in its table, but q008 does not name the bar or mass matrix. Every numeric key in all units (weak form, Ritz/Galerkin, Jacobians, Gauss rules, quality metrics, triangle strains, beam and shear ratios, shell stresses, thermal assembly and stability limits, restrained-bar stresses, bar eigenvalues, central-difference steps, Newton-Raphson table, penalty contact, Richardson/GCI, verification checks) was recomputed and agrees with its key and tolerance. No tabs, control characters, format placeholders, e-notation numbers, plain x in LaTeX, placeholder steps or stale option-letter references were found. Only one minor clarity issue remains. This is an AI review only; the course still needs a subject-matter expert before engineering reliance.

The lesson table rounds the lumped first-mode error to -2.6% while q005/q010 say 2.5%, so the rounded figures differ across the unit.
